title: Loadsmith: tenant-aware throughput certification framework and customer acceptance scenarios
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Build a repeatable, tenant-aware throughput certification framework (Loadsmith) and associated customer acceptance scenarios. The framework must produce deterministic evidence (telemetry exports, run artifacts, signatures) for throughput guarantees and autoscaler policy behavior across Dedicated clusters, and make it simple for solutions teams to run acceptance tests with customer-replay or synthetic proxies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Loadsmith can run tenant-aware replay and synthetic mixes against a Dedicated pool and produce a signed evidence bundle (telemetry, run id, config snapshot).

2) For a representative set of workloads (chat short, chat long, embeddings mixed), documented SLO/thresholds are evaluated: p95 latency <= 150ms, p99 latency <= 500ms, sustained QPS within +/-5% of target for 10m steady window.

3) Autoscaler policy behavior is validated: scale-up occurs within configured window under sustained pressure; scale-down respects cooldowns and does not oscillate with tenant churn. Evidence shows no SLA violations during policy transitions.
4) Tenant isolation test passes: noisy-tenant injection does not degrade other tenants beyond defined QoS knobs (max 15% latency uplift at p95).
5) Run artifacts exported to customer-facing acceptance bundle and validated by Solutions Engineer checklist.
technical_approach: Loadsmith is a modular harness: (a) replay driver that accepts parquet traces or live traffic capture, (b) synthetic profile generator with configurable burstiness, sequence length and cache-warm flags, (c) orchestrator that schedules cross-tenant mixes against a target Dedicated pool with config capture, and (d) evidence packager that captures telemetry, sample requests/responses, kernel selection logs, and autoscaler events. It will integrate with existing fleet telemetry (Prometheus/OTLP) and Console artifacts (trace links, per-model breakdowns).
test_plan: 1) Define benchmark profiles: short-chat (avg tokens=40), long-chat (avg tokens=1200), embeddings-bulk (vector size 1536, batch sizes 64/128). 2) For each profile run three phases: ramp (5m), steady-state (10m), ramp-down (5m). 3) Execute tenant-isolation scenario by adding a noisy tenant generating microbursts. 4) Validate autoscaler by artificially constraining capacity and observing scale events. 5) Run warm-cache and cold-cache variants to measure KV cache impact. 6) Collect metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained qps, tokens/s, model variant fallbacks, kernel selection distribution, GPU utilization, and allocator/queue lengths. 7) Produce evidence bundle with run-id, config snapshot, and telemetry exports. 8) Provide a reproducible script and Docker image for customers to run locally or in their VPC.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha runs on staging Dedicated pools with engineering + SRE and iterate on artifacts. Phase 2: Beta with 2 pilot customers using replayed workloads and joint validation call. Phase 3: General availability with Console integration (one-click acceptance bundle generation). Each customer pilot includes a 2-week onboarding window and a final acceptance signoff by Solutions + Engineering.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff; confirmed scope with PM; initial list of benchmark profiles agreed.
2026-02-22: Proof-of-concept replay driver produced; can consume rewritten request parquet and drive tokens through staging runtime.
2026-02-28: Synthetic profile generator done; added jitter and burstiness knobs for realistic microbursts.
2026-03-05: First steady-state runs executed against staging Dedicated pool; discovered autoscaler cooldown was too aggressive causing delayed scale-up.
2026-03-09: Autoscaler tuning PR opened to add an aggressive burst-policy flag for certification runs (PR #2317).
customer_acceptance_checklist: Customer replay runs successfully in their VPC or via obfuscated trace
Acceptance bundle verified by Solutions Engineer
SLA metrics meet documented thresholds for the customer's target profiles
Signed run report uploaded to customer's artifact folder
Post-run support handoff completed with SRE and Solutions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Replay fidelity mismatch with production -> Mitigation: provide SDK adapters and a small 'sanity replay' that validates trace mapping before full run.
Risk: Autoscaler flaps during synthetic microbursts -> Mitigation: introduce canary policy with burst-capacity hold and require manual approval for permanent policy changes.
Risk: Evidence bundle size/privacy concerns -> Mitigation: default scrubber for PII and opt-in verbose artifacts for customers with NDA.
